newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - French lead European equity markets higher.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - French lead European equity markets higher.

text.p: French shares led European equities higher to a buoyant close on Thursday, the Paris bourse climbing more than two percent as investors reacted with relief at the makeup of the new left-wing government.
All three of the main European share markets in London, Paris and Frankfurt ended with gains, while Swiss shares posted their third consecutive record close.
The dollar was mired in tiny ranges against the mark in late European trade as dealers focused on Friday's scheduled release of key monthly employment reports from the United States and Germany.

Uncertainties shrouding the shape, size and timing of the single European currency lost centre stage to these economic reports. But a lack of consensus about their likely impact confined the dollar to established bands.
"The political row in Europe is in many respects ambiguous for the mark and the impact of German economic data is finely balanced," said Paul Meggyesi at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Palladium prices swung wildly as market makers held crisis talks on severe shortages of the precious metal because of a halt to Russian exports.
It closed at $210.00 an ounce after hitting $235.00 in the morning, its highest fixing since the twice-daily fix began in 1989.
"It's a hairy situation...Volatility is huge today," said analyst Nick Moore of Flemings Global Mining Group.
The crisis prompted market makers to suspend the market in forward palladium after one-month lease rates shot up to 300 percent on Wednesday night.
In the equity markets most drama was in Paris. The CAC-40 index surged more three percent at one point to break the 2,700 point barrier, although the froth came off the market in the afternoon.
By the close the CAC was up 55.48 points, or 2.11 percent, at 2,690.85.

Traders said investors had been reassured by the make-up of the government, with the appointment of Dominique Strauss-Kahn as Finance Minister and only one communist getting a big portfolio at transport.
"The rise was a bit exaggerated. I think we'll see a bit of consolidation tomorrow," one trader said.

Despite lingering concerns over European economic and monetary union (EMU) and Germany's budget problems, Frankfurt share traders voiced relief at the apparent settlement of Bonn's dispute with the Bundesbank over revaluing the nation's reserves.

"The important thing is that they seem to have found an amicable solution," said Josh Waiblinger, assistant vice president of equities at BHF-Bank, as the DAX index put on 11 points in bourse trade. The IBIS DAX ended 33 points higher in later screen trade.
Airline Deutsche Lufthansa hit a record high of 30.90 marks, a rise of 1.40 marks, with traders citing a positive U.S. research paper. The German carrier closed at 30.80 marks.
British shares finished higher for the first time in seven sessions as renewed bid speculation swirled around dealing rooms in London's "Square Mile" financial district.
As European markets closed, the Dow Jones Industrial Average was up around 60 points, also giving the market a much needed boost.
"Talk of predators on the prowl pushed the market up today," one senior dealer said. "The stories going around are old but the old ones are sometimes the best ones."
The FTSE 100 ended 19.1 points higher to 4,576.2.
Abbey National Plc hit a high of 852p before closing at 843-1/2, up 16-1/2p on continued speculation that National Westminster Bank Plc was considering making a bid.
Investors will be watching Bank of England money market operations on Friday to see if the bank's new monetary committee, which met on Thursday, decided to push up British interest rates.

"The chance for a rate hike is finely balanced. If we don't get a hike and if the U.S. numbers are in-line, we could see the FTSE push well above 4,600 tomorrow," the head of trading at a large brokerage said.
CURRENCIES AT 1600 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.7300 marks and 115.68 yen compared with 1.7310 marks and 116.23 yen in late European trading on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS CLOSING PRICES
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index closed up 19.1 points, or 0.42 percent, at 4,576.2.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 55.48 points, or 2.11 percent, at 2,690.85.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed up 11.19 points, or 0.31 percent, at 3,673.03. In later screen-based trade, the IBIS DAX ended up 33.01 points at 3,673.03.
PRECIOUS METALS

Palladium closed at $210.00 against $235.00 after forward quoting was suspended. Platinum ended at $435, up $3.00. Gold finished at $341.75, down 60 cents, while silver closed four cents higher at $4.80.
